It is nothing short of a gaming masterpiece that delivers an adrenaline-fueled experience, blending intense combat, strategic gameplay, and the thrill of emerging victorious in a battle royale setting.  From the moment you parachute onto the diverse and expansive maps, PUBG immerses you in a world where survival is not just a goal but a relentless pursuit. The realistic graphics and attention to detail create an atmosphere that is both visually stunning and tactically challenging. Every footstep, gunshot, and rustle in the distance adds to the suspense, making each match a heart-pounding adventure.  One of PUBG's standout features is its commitment to realism. The gun mechanics are meticulously designed, requiring players to master recoil control and bullet drop for effective long-range engagements. This attention to detail extends to the environmental factors, including weather changes and dynamic terrain, ensuring that no two matches feel the same.  The game's expansive player base ensures quick matchmaking, and whether you prefer the solo experience, teaming up with a duo, or coordinating with a squad, PUBG offers versatile gameplay options. Teamwork and communication are paramount, creating a social aspect that enhances the overall gaming experience.  PUBG's commitment to staying relevant is evident through regular updates and additions. The developers introduce new maps, weapons, and gameplay enhancements, keeping the community engaged and excited for what's next. The evolving esports scene adds another layer of competitiveness, offering players the chance to showcase their skills on a global stage.  The variety of maps, each with its own unique challenges, adds a strategic element to the game. Whether navigating the dense forests of Erangel or battling it out in the urban sprawl of Sanhok, every location demands adaptability and tactical thinking.  In conclusion, PUBG on Steam is a must-play for anyone seeking a challenging and immersive battle royale experience. Its realistic gameplay, dynamic environments, and vibrant community make it a standout title in the genre. Prepare for the adrenaline rush, the heart-stopping moments, and the sweet taste of victory in PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds.

Chicken Shawarma  Ingredients for four people: Chicken fillet 400 g Parsley 50 g Pickled cucumber 6 Potatoes (optional) 2 Pita bread 4 (or as needed) Olive oil 3 tbsp Onion 1 Parmesan cheese 100 g Salt 2 tbsp Turmeric 1 tsp Ground black pepper 2 tsp Garlic powder 2 tsp  Ingredients for tahini sauce: Thick yogurt 4 tbsp Mayonnaise 1 tbsp Tahini 1 tbsp Fresh lemon juice 3 tbsp Garlic 1 Salt 1 tsp (or to taste) Ground black pepper ½ tsp (or to taste)  Wash the chicken fillet, take the chicken skin off and slice them into strips. Add them to a mixing bowl.  Mix up the salt, turmeric, black pepper, and garlic powder. Add them along with the olive oil to the Chicken and massage the seasoning into the chicken fillets.  Cut the onion into slices and add them to the Chicken. Mix everything together.  Cover the Chicken with a plastic film and let it sit in the fridge for at least an hour. Chilling the mixture will marinate the Chicken and infuse it with flavor.  While the Chicken is marinating, prepare the tahini sauce. For this purpose, pour the thick yogurt with mayonnaise, tahini, lemon juice, salt, and black pepper into a suitable bowl.  Finely grate the garlic and add it to the bowl. Then mix until the sauce is uniform. Note that the sauce should be as thick as porridge.  Now put a suitable pan on low heat and coat it with oil. Once the oil is hot enough, add the marinated chicken fillets into the pan and sauté until the fillets change color.  Meanwhile, you can fry the potatoes. Slice the potato lengthwise to your desired thickness.  Put a pan on the heat and add two to three tablespoons of oil. Then fry the potatoes in oil over medium heat until they get golden.  Wash the parsley and drain the excess water. Now transfer them to a tray and chop them finely.  Place the pita bread on your tray. Take the tahini sauce and spread it on the center of the bread.  Pile a layer of the chicken fillets, fried potatoes, chopped pickles, parsley, and a sprinkle of parmesan cheese on the bread and roll it. You can top the ingredient with tahini sauce if you like.  At this stage, preheat the sandwich maker, then roast the shawarmas in the machine. In the absence of a sandwich maker, place an unoiled grill pan on medium heat and put the shawarmas in the pan. Then put a heavy object on them to grill them thoroughly.  Once the shawarmas are roasted, and the bread is crispy, cut them in half and put them in your desired dish. You do not have to eat shawarma with bread if you want to stay away from carbohydrates, and you can serve them with salad or plain.  Enjoy your meal!

PUBG, or 'Pan Unknown's Battle Groceries,' as I like to call it, is the ultimate virtual shopping experience gone wild. Imagine this: you're parachuted onto a remote island with nothing but a shopping list. Your mission? To gather groceries while avoiding being turned into a human kebab by fellow shoppers. The supermarket is your battleground, and the aisles are your trenches.  Forget peaceful shopping. Here, it's all about grabbing that last can of beans like it's a gold bar in Fort Knox. And if you're lucky enough to find the frying pan, congratulations, you're now the Iron Chef of combat cookery. It's a game of hide-and-seek, but instead of hiding behind curtains, you're crouching in a bush with a sniper rifle, eyeing the frozen food section.  You'll form alliances only to have them crumble over who gets the last pack of ramen. And just when you think you've got a moment to breathe and admire the picturesque sunset, you remember there's a deadly force field shrinking around you, pushing everyone into the ultimate food fight finale. Title: A Battle Royale Masterpiece  Rating: ★★★★★  Reviewer: Raiyan0628  Tactical Gameplay: PUBG demands a level of tactical awareness rarely seen in gaming. Players must constantly adapt to the ever-shrinking safe zone, forcing engagements that require strategic thinking and quick decision-making.  Team Coordination: Communication and teamwork are paramount. Effective coordination with your squad can be the difference between victory and defeat. This mirrors the critical importance of teamwork in real-world military operations. Realistic Weaponry: The arsenal in PUBG is meticulously crafted, mirroring real-world firearms. Understanding the ballistics and recoil patterns adds a layer of authenticity to the gameplay.  Pros: Realism and Immersion: PUBG excels in creating an immersive battlefield experience. The realistic environments, coupled with authentic sound design, make every firefight feel visceral and intense. Continuous Development: The development team consistently updates the game, introducing new maps, weapons, and gameplay mechanics. This commitment to improvement keeps the experience fresh and engaging. Diverse Map Selection: From the dense forests of Erangel to the desert expanses of Miramar, each map offers a unique and dynamic battleground, ensuring no two matches feel the same. Global Player Base: With millions of players worldwide, PUBG offers a vibrant and competitive community. Whether you're a casual gamer or aspiring esports pro, there's a place for you in this expansive player base. Customization and Cosmetics: The game provides an extensive array of customization options, allowing players to personalize their characters and weapons, adding a touch of individuality to the battlefield.  Cons:  Learning Curve: PUBG has a steep learning curve, especially for newcomers. Mastering the mechanics and map knowledge takes time and patience. Optimization: While PUBG has made significant strides in optimization, it can still be demanding on hardware. Players with lower-end systems may experience performance issues.  PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds on Steam stands as a testament to the potential of the battle royale genre. Its emphasis on realism, tactical gameplay, and team coordination creates an experience that resonates with military analysts like myself. With a thriving player base and continuous development, PUBG remains a powerhouse in the gaming world.

OK, so I played this game back in 2018 when it was pretty new and was not free-to-play.  I came from the DayZ mod, where gameplay was slow and careful, weapons and resources were extremely rare, and you could lose everything very quickly by getting too close to a group of zombies or encountering an unfriendly player.  PUBG was a completely different kettle of fish, where some of the elements of DayZ had been distilled into shorter play sessions, where the action was frenetic and somewhat stressful.  Picking your jump point from the plane, the descent to your chosen area and the initial desperate search for weapons and supplies, were all elements that injected something new.    The weapons were realistic and had various attachments that would enhance them, so you were always on the lookout for something to improve what you already had.  The blue electrical field that kept moving in, decreasing the safe space on the island, was great at forcing players out of places where they were hiding.  I remember the stress of hiding inside a building, hearing someone outside come in and start to search the property, knowing that there was possibly someone inside.

As of 2023 I wouldn't recommend that any of my friends play PUBG.

Gameplay (8/10): PUBG is known for its intense and realistic battle royale gameplay. It offers a large open world where up to 100 players parachute onto an island and compete to be the last person or team standing. The game emphasizes strategic planning, teamwork, and precise shooting. The variety of weapons, vehicles, and attachments adds depth to the gameplay.  Graphics and Visuals (7/10): PUBG featured detailed and realistic environments, but it wasn't always the most visually impressive game, especially when compared to newer titles. However, the game had undergone graphical improvements over time to enhance its visual quality.  Maps (8/10): PUBG originally launched with a single map, Erangel, and later introduced several other maps, each with its own unique terrain and challenges. The maps offered a variety of environments, from dense forests to urban areas, providing different gameplay experiences.  Community and Updates (8/10): The PUBG community was active, and the developers regularly released updates and patches to address bugs, introduce new content, and balance gameplay. Seasonal passes and events kept players engaged, and the game maintained a dedicated player base.  Performance (7/10): PUBG's performance could be somewhat inconsistent, especially on lower-end hardware. While it was generally well-optimized, some players experienced issues with frame rates and server lag. The game did require a relatively powerful PC to run smoothly.  Microtransactions (7/10): PUBG featured microtransactions primarily for cosmetic items like skins and clothing. While these microtransactions didn't affect gameplay, some players felt that certain cosmetic items were priced too high.  Community and Esports (8/10): PUBG had a competitive esports scene, with major tournaments and events attracting top players and teams. The community also organized various tournaments and leagues, contributing to its longevity.  Conclusion: PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds played a pivotal role in popularizing the battle royale genre and offered a unique and engaging experience for players who enjoyed tactical and realistic gameplay. It had its share of technical issues and performance challenges, but the game's frequent updates and community engagement helped it remain a popular choice among battle royale enthusiasts.

"PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS - Where My Chicken Dinner Awaits... Somewhere"  Rating: ★★★★☆  PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS, the game where I've learned that getting a chicken dinner isn't just about skill; it's about surviving the most bizarre, hilarious, and utterly chaotic scenarios imaginable.  Pros:  - I've become a master of improvisation. Need a getaway vehicle? A frying pan? A human shield? No problem, I've got it covered. - The game's realism is so immersive that I've started looting my neighbor's houses for supplies during power outages. Who needs electricity when you have bandages and energy drinks? - I've developed a knack for deciphering the subtle nuances of my teammates' communication, even when it consists of nothing but panicked screaming and laughter. - PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS has provided me with countless "Only in PUBG" moments that make for legendary stories. Like the time I won a firefight using only a crossbow and sheer luck.  Cons:  - My sense of time has gone out the window. "Just one more game" easily turns into "Oh, it's 4 AM, and I have work in a few hours." - I've suffered from "PUBG Paranoia," where I've shot at bushes, rocks, and shadows, convinced they were enemy players. Spoiler: Most of the time, they weren't. - My friends now identify me by my in-game nickname more than my real name. "Hey, PUBGPro123, pass me that ammo." - I've developed an irrational fear of red zones. I'll take on a squad of enemy players any day, but a barrage of virtual bombs? No thanks. - PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is like a rollercoaster ride through a war zone, complete with adrenaline-pumping firefights, absurdly wild vehicle stunts, and the constant fear of being sniped while taking cover behind a tree.  To those contemplating their next drop: Embrace the chaos, cherish the moments, and remember that it's not about the chicken dinner; it's about the crazy journey to get there.  In conclusion, PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is where I've learned that in the battleground of life, it's important to have a sense of humor and a Level 3 helmet.  Overall rating: ★★★★☆

PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds (PUBG) - це гра, яка революціонізувала жанр "битви королів" (battle royale) і назавжди залишила слід у світі відеоігор. PUBG приніс битви на великому острові, де сотні гравців змагаються на виживання, і це стало однією з найбільш захоплюючих ігор останнього десятиліття.  Однією з ключових особливостей PUBG є його реалістична графіка і фізика, які створюють неймовірно іммерсивний світ. Кожен елемент гри, від зброї до автомобілів, має свою унікальну фізичну модель, що додає відчуття реалізму і стратегії до гри. Розробники регулярно оновлюють гру, додаючи новий контент і вдосконалюючи графічний рівень, щоб завжди забезпечувати якісний ігровий досвід.  Битви в PUBG завжди непередбачувані і захоплюючі. Ви можете грати самотужки, у парі або в команді з друзями, і кожен бій завжди приносить нові виклики та сюрпризи. Ігрова карта розміром 8x8 кілометрів робить кожен матч унікальним і вимагає від гравців стратегічного мислення та тактичної спритності.  Крім того, спільнота гравців PUBG є однією з найбільших та найактивніших у світі відеоігор. Гра має велику кількість послуг та турнірів, де гравці можуть випробувати свої навички та змагатися за призи.  Узагалі, PUBG - це гра, яка вразить вас своєю глибиною, стратегічністю і неймовірною напругою на протязі всієї гри. Ця гра встановила високі стандарти для жанру "битви королів" і продовжує залишати свій слід в історії відеоігор. Якщо ви шукаєте ігру, яка вас викликає і вразить своєю глибиною, PUBG - це те, що вам потрібно спробувати.

Of all the BR games that I've played, none *feel* as well rounded as this one. Sure, the skill gap is sharp. It's supposed to be. However; the thing that makes PUBG my favorite BR is the gunplay. You can win the game with ANY weapon. There are meta weapons, like the AUG or M4, but you are not required to use them, nor do you need a specialized loadout (cough, cough Warzone) to win gun fights.  The only thing I can say that isn't so great about this game is the revive system. At the current moment of writing this there are 3 different Revive Systems, each on their own respective maps. Ideally, there should be just one to stick to so as to not confuse new players. The most promising of these thus far is the Blue Chip revive system, which has it's flaws, but is better than the Mini BRs between zones for redeployment. No, they aren't like the Gulag at all.  I recommend this game to anyone who wants a more blood pumping, semi realistic style BR. No crouch sliding try hards, no insta heal shield batteries, no ground-lootable OP gun spawns. Just a good ol' boots to the ground, assymetric level playing field and loot.  Opinion may vary from the time of writing, may update later.

PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds (PUBG) stands as an iconic pioneer in the battle royale genre, delivering an intense and exhilarating gaming experience that has captured the hearts of millions worldwide. With its innovative gameplay mechanics, strategic depth, and heart-pounding moments, PUBG has solidified its position as a must-play title that continues to evolve and impress.  PUBG's core gameplay revolves around the electrifying battle royale formula that has become a cultural phenomenon. Dropping onto an expansive map with nothing but the clothes on your back, the rush to find weapons, gear, and supplies in a shrinking play zone is both nerve-wracking and addictively fun. The tension builds with every step, and each engagement is a test of skill, strategy, and quick decision-making.  The game's map design is a masterstroke, offering diverse landscapes that cater to different playstyles. From the urban chaos of city centers to the serene isolation of rural areas, each location presents unique opportunities and challenges. The balance between open spaces and tight environments ensures that every match is a dynamic and unpredictable experience, keeping players on their toes.  What truly sets PUBG apart is its emphasis on strategy and tactical decision-making. Every match requires careful consideration of positioning, movement, and engagement timing. The intricate ballistics system adds a layer of realism, rewarding players who master the nuances of bullet drop and travel time. Whether you prefer stealthy approaches, aggressive rushes, or cunning traps, PUBG accommodates a variety of playstyles, allowing you to shape your own path to victory.  The adrenaline-pumping moments in PUBG are nothing short of legendary. The exhilaration of narrowly escaping an ambush, the satisfaction of securing a hard-fought kill, and the intensity of a final showdown in the shrinking circle create memories that are etched into players' minds. Each match is a story of survival, and the journey to victory is paved with unforgettable highs and heart-stopping lows.  PUBG's commitment to constant improvement and innovation is commendable. Regular updates bring new content, balance adjustments, and quality-of-life enhancements that keep the game fresh and exciting. The addition of different maps, game modes, and limited-time events ensures that the experience is constantly evolving, inviting players to return for new challenges and experiences.  The graphics and audio design in PUBG contribute to its immersive atmosphere. The attention to detail in the environments, weapon models, and character animations creates a gritty and realistic world that draws players in. The ambient sounds, from distant gunfire to footsteps in the grass, add an extra layer of immersion and strategic value, helping players anticipate the movements of their opponents.  In conclusion, PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds is a true marvel of the gaming world. Its blend of tension, strategy, and pulse-pounding action creates an experience that is both addictive and rewarding. PUBG's ability to foster unforgettable moments, its commitment to evolution, and its vibrant global community make it a game that transcends trends and remains a staple in the battle royale genre. Whether you're a hardcore gamer seeking strategic challenges or a casual player looking for high-octane excitement, PUBG is a journey worth embarking on.

I recommend it, because it's fun to hop into a party with friends and hang out/chat while you await your inevitable death.  My friends and I mostly used it as an excuse to just do something together online.  If that's all you care about, and you don't care about winning, go nuts.  However, the game itself is a mess. Buggy and inconsistent. Vehicle mechanics are a nightmare.  Jumping/movement feels clunky, even with hundreds of hours playing.  Winning a match that isn't filled with bots is pretty damn difficult, though I do have a few wins, and they do feel incredible when they happen.  That said, a large amount of who will in boils down to who finds the best scopes and guns first, in many cases. Sometimes you just can't find good equipment, and unlike other games in the genre, that pretty much seals your fate.  The game prides itself on realism (bullets have physics affected by distance, etc), but they've started trying to compete with Fortnite by having weird costumes, which makes the overall aesthetic just kind of all over the place.  Do they want realism, or a weird goofy deathmatch?  It seems like they're at a point where they can't pick a lane.  There are simply much better games in the genre that control so much better and feel more satisfying to play.  But my friends and I had a lot of good laughs mixed throughout all the frustration, so if you set the bar low you'll probably have some fun.  Just don't expect to win many rounds unless you dedicate your life to improving your skills (or you get exceptionally lucky).

I don't even remember the last time this game got an update that actually added anything significant. So far this year, there's been at least eight "major" updates and I believe all of them were just new cosmetics, with no new changes to gameplay or added features. While this might work for games like CS:GO, which never gets any significant updates, but does occasionally add skins, it doesn't work for PUBG. It's hard to explain exactly why this is, but if you ask me it's probably because CS:GO doesn't feel as though it needs improvements, and because the skins in CS:GO actually look nice, whereas the ones in PUBG look like drawings made by a five year old. One of the problems with PUBG's updates is that each update typically takes eight gigabytes of space or more on your computer (and you are required to download these updates to play the game), all for a few skins which both look like shit and make you easier to spot from a distance in-game, which literally gives you a disadvantage. It also seems that the developers put more effort into the mobile version rather than the original, which clearly shows that they only care about making profit instead of a good game. Overall, it's really just disappointing how this game has gone to shit, as the gameplay was actually fun and offered something unique in it's genre. I have enjoyed this game and I do think it still can be enjoyable, but I certainly wouldn't recommend to anyone (regardless of it's price) considering it's current state.

PUBG Team    I am writing to you today as an avid player, a fervent supporter, and a committed guardian of fair play within the world of Player Unknown's Battleground. For years, I have taken it upon myself to maintain the integrity of our shared digital landscape by identifying and reporting instances of cheating that threaten to undermine the experience we all hold dear.  I have stood sentinel, constantly vigilant in my watch over the community. My service, although a labor of love, has been a time-intensive and often unacknowledged task. Still, I have always felt an unwavering sense of duty to protect the sanctity of our game, its rules, and its spirit, ensuring that all players are granted an equitable, fair, and rewarding gaming experience.  Over the years, I've filed numerous reports, provided countless pieces of evidence, and dedicated many hours to helping improve the anti-cheat system. I've done so out of a deeply rooted love for the game, a respect for the community, and a belief that every player should have an equal and fair opportunity to succeed.  Although I have done this voluntarily, I write to you today to consider the concept of compensation. The hours I have spent identifying and reporting cheaters represent a significant commitment. And while the personal satisfaction of preserving fairness is a reward in itself, I believe some form of recognition or compensation would be appropriate and encouraging not just for me, but for others who might follow in these footsteps.  This compensation need not necessarily be financial. There are many ways to acknowledge the work of loyal players like me, such as exclusive in-game items, unique badges, additional season pass benefits, or a tiered system of rewards tied to the number of verified cheat reports. This would not only serve as an acknowledgment of our efforts but also as an incentive for more players to join the anti-cheat crusade, consequently enhancing the integrity of our beloved game.  I'd also like to suggest the possibility of forming an official volunteer anti-cheat team. This team could be composed of dedicated players who have demonstrated a commitment to maintaining the game's integrity, like myself. We could provide valuable feedback and suggestions to improve the game's anti-cheat measures based on our extensive hands-on experience.  In conclusion, I kindly request you to consider these proposals. I believe that acknowledging the efforts of players like me could foster a more engaged and vigilant community, encourage fair play, and ultimately contribute to making Player Unknown's Battleground the best gaming experience it can be.  I look forward to your response and the possibility of working even more closely with you to protect and enhance the game that has become such a significant part of our lives. Still, I have always felt an unwavering sense of duty to protect the sanctity of our game, its rules, and its spirit, ensuring that all players are granted an equitable, fair, and rewarding gaming experience.  Over the years, I've filed numerous reports, provided countless pieces of evidence, and dedicated many hours to helping improve the anti-cheat system. I've done so out of a deeply rooted love for the game, a respect for the community, and a belief that every player should have an equal and fair opportunity to succeed.  Although I have done this voluntarily, I write to you today to consider the concept of compensation. The hours I have spent identifying and reporting cheaters represent a significant commitment. And while the personal satisfaction of preserving fairness is a reward in itself, I believe some form of recognition or compensation would be appropriate and encouraging not just for me, but for others who might follow in these footsteps.  This compensation need not necessarily be financial. There are many ways to acknowledge the work of loyal players like me, such as exclusive in-game items, unique badges, additional season pass benefits, or a tiered system of rewards tied to the number of verified cheat reports. This would not only serve as an acknowledgment of our efforts but also as an incentive for more players to join the anti-cheat crusade, consequently enhancing the integrity of our beloved game.  I'd also like to suggest the possibility of forming an official volunteer anti-cheat team. This team could be composed of dedicated players who have demonstrated a commitment to maintaining the game's integrity, like myself. We could provide valuable feedback and suggestions to improve the game's anti-cheat measures based on our extensive hands-on experience.  In conclusion, I kindly request you to consider these proposals. I believe that acknowledging the efforts of players like me could foster a more engaged and vigilant community, encourage fair play, and ultimately contribute to making Player Unknown's Battleground the best gaming experience it can be.  I look forward to your response and the possibility of working even more closely with you to protect and enhance the game that has become such a significant part of our lives. I've been playing PUBG since August 2017 when it was in Early Access, so I consider myself a veteran at this game. This, plus the amount of time I've spent playing it and the tens of chicken dinners I've gotten over the years qualify me to say that this game is.. pretty fun. Honestly, It has a ton of content. So many weapons and vehicles, great maps (except for Miramar), loot, firefights, this game has it all. In my opinion PUBG was and still is the king of battle royale. You can't go wrong with this instant classic.   The only problems I would consider this game to have would be the bugs and the performance. I'm pretty sure KRAFTON is porting this game to UE5, so at this point it makes sense to not be a stellar focus for the studio. Perhaps the engine update will help with both issues, though I personally find it unlikely. But still, even with these issues considered, I would recommend this game to a group of FPS players. Seriously, you can't go wrong with the insane dopamine and adrenaline rush you get in this game, nothing comes close to an intense firefight being won by superior tactics and communication with your mates.  TL;DR A PC classic.

With its strategic gameplay, diverse maps, and intense firefights, this game has undoubtedly secured its place as one of the best in the genre.  [b]Land, Loot, Survive![/b] The game's core concept revolves around the three essential elements: land, loot, and survive. From the moment you parachute onto the map, you're thrust into a world brimming with possibilities. Whether you prefer to drop into a hot zone for a chaotic firefight or opt for a more strategic approach, the choice is yours.  [b]Thrilling Battlegrounds[/b] PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS boasts an impressive array of diverse and meticulously designed battlegrounds. Each map presents its own unique challenges and opportunities, from the sprawling fields of Erangel to the dense urban environment of Miramar. The attention to detail in the environments is remarkable, providing an immersive experience that truly transports you into the heart of the action.  [b]Team up and Dominate[/b] Squad up with friends or join forces with strangers in intense 100-player battles, as you strive to outlast and outgun your opponents. The teamwork required to secure victory adds an extra layer of depth to the gameplay, fostering unforgettable moments of camaraderie and triumph. Communication and coordination are key, making each match an exhilarating test of skill and strategy.  [b]Weapons and Supplies[/b] The thrill of PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS lies in its vast arsenal of weapons and the pursuit of valuable supplies. Scour the map for firearms, attachments, armor, and healing items to ensure your survival in the face of relentless adversaries. The game strikes a delicate balance, offering a wide range of equipment without overwhelming the player, allowing for both strategic planning and quick decision-making during intense firefights.  [b]Visually Stunning[/b] PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is a visual feast for the eyes. The graphics are nothing short of breathtaking, with detailed environments, realistic lighting, and smooth animations. From the moment you step foot onto the battleground, you'll be captivated by the game's immersive visuals, which enhance the overall gameplay experience.  [b]Constant Updates[/b] The development team behind PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is dedicated to providing a top-notch experience for players. Regular updates bring new features, gameplay enhancements, and optimizations, ensuring the game remains fresh and exciting. The commitment to continuous improvement demonstrates the developers' passion for their creation and their dedication to providing a high-quality gaming experience.  [b]Conclusion[/b] PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS has solidified itself as a must-play title in the Battle Royale genre. With its strategic gameplay, diverse and immersive battlegrounds, and a dedicated development team, it offers an unparalleled gaming experience. Whether you're a fan of intense firefights, teamwork, or the thrill of being the last one standing, this game has it all. Join the Battlegrounds and embark on an epic adventure that will keep you coming back for more.

Well, what to say about this game? It is certainly a mixed bag, infuriating at times, and just awesome sometimes. Bought this game when it came out back in the day and played a bit on the Nvidia Geforce Now beta since I didn't have a PC. Then I bought to Xbox and struggled through 2000+ hours of a terrible port. horrible graphics, framerate that dropped to 5 fps when you were in close combat or driving a car, and a loot system on control that was just super awkward...  But the concept of every match being "unique" in some sense just blew me away. Where do you drop? what do you find (you remember when you could run into a house and just find clothes that spawned?!)? Who's dropping next to you, where does the circle go, etc? Combined with a brutal no-training mode/introduction gameplay was just my cup of tea.  Eventually, I sold my console and forgot about this game until I got myself a decent PC this year and picked it up again. Now it's funny emotes, dances, crazy clothes, new maps, a lot of bots, and an actual training mode (for the first few matches at least), most of the time you can choose your gear due to the hugely increased spawn rate.   So it certainly feels a bit more accessible but I still enjoy it and have gotten a few 100 hours of gameplay so far.   All in all, buy the game and suffer like the rest of us, it's annoying, too many sweaty players, unfair zones, mistakes are made, and team communication will break down but if you prevail a chicken dinner is like no other dinner.

Rating: ★★★★☆  PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS, developed by PUBG Corporation, is a side-splittingly hilarious game that combines intense battle royale action, strategic camping, and a whole lot of absurd firefights. If you've ever wanted to experience the thrill of outwitting opponents, hiding in bathtubs, and laughing your way through ridiculously chaotic battles, then grab your frying pan, hop onto the nearest loot truck, and prepare for a laughter-filled battle royale like no other!  The premise of PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is both thrilling and ridiculously entertaining. You find yourself on a remote island, armed with nothing but your wits and a burning desire to be the last person standing. But here's the catch: you're dropped into a vast map with 99 other players who are equally determined to secure that elusive chicken dinner. Picture this: you're hiding in a bathroom, clutching a shotgun, while the sound of footsteps gets closer. Suddenly, a player bursts in, sees you sitting in the tub, and a hilariously awkward firefight ensues. It's a comedy of errors and unpredictable encounters that will have you rolling on the floor with laughter.  The game's immersive environments and dynamic gameplay contribute to its comedic appeal. From looting houses and stumbling upon bizarre combinations of weaponry to driving vehicles in the most hilariously reckless manner, PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS never fails to create moments of pure chaos and laughter. It's a game where even the most carefully crafted strategies can crumble into a hilarious mess with a single wrong move or a well-placed banana peel.  PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS' iconic frying pan and its absurd effectiveness in close combat are a source of endless amusement. Watching players engage in frantic battles, wielding frying pans as if they were medieval weapons, adds a delightful touch of humor to the game. Who knew that a humble cooking utensil could be so hilariously lethal?  The game's community and their creativity in finding unconventional ways to have fun further add to its comedic value. From organizing absurd events like motorcycle races through impossible terrain to dressing up in outlandish outfits and creating impromptu dance parties in the middle of a firefight, the PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS community knows how to find laughter in even the most intense moments.  While PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS' competitive nature and occasional frustrations can be overwhelming, it's precisely those moments that make the comedic highlights all the more enjoyable. It's a game that embraces the absurdity of its battles, inviting you to find humor in the most dire situations. From epic shootouts ending with a well-timed punch to the hilarity of driving a vehicle into a lake while your teammates scream in panic, PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS provides a laughter-filled battleground that you won't soon forget.  In conclusion, PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is a hilariously entertaining game that combines intense battle royale action with moments of pure comedy gold. With its dynamic gameplay, unexpected encounters, and the sheer absurdity of its firefights, it offers an unforgettable and laughter-filled experience. If you're looking for a game that will test your survival skills, challenge your strategic thinking, and provide endless moments of mirth and mayhem, PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is the ultimate comedic battleground extravaganza that guarantees laughter, chicken dinners, and an unforgettable battle royale experience.

I work at a local grocery store stocking shelves. I work morning shifts, which means I am unloading the trucks of product that come in and I’m usually the only person to handle that product until I put it on store shelves. A pretty mundane job, until one day when I hear of the Rock’s new energy drink Zoa, able to gift the power of the Rock onto any drinker. This is significant, because if I knew that eventually our store would start selling Zoa, and who would be unloading it off the truck before any customers could get to it? Me. All I had to do was wait.   Well, today was the day! The truck came in at around 6:07am and I was ready for it. As soon as the truck doors opened, I searched each and every pallet for the boxes contained Zoa energy drink. As I found the boxes that contained it, I had to stop myself from tearing into the box and guzzling the liquid right then and there! I knew that Zoa was a slow acting drink, and that though it offers limitless power, it would be best for me to wait until I could make a clean getaway. I hid the boxes in a corner of the receiving area under some out of use promotional signs, away from prying eyes. I went about the rest of my shift practically jumping with excitement. One I clocked out, I was able to smuggle the boxes out of the store by hiding it under the ridiculously large coats the store forces employees to wear. Eventually, I had done it! Every box of Zoa was in my car, and I was home free.   52 cans. I got home four hours ago and in the time since I have devoured every last drop of Zoa energy drink. 52 cans are now empty. It started with my fingertips. They tingled in a way I had never felt before. I reached out and grasped by phone, and it felt… more. More than I had ever felt. This feeling eventually spread throughout my body, to the point where I was feeling even the clothes on my skin. Panicking due to the sensory overload, I threw my phone down and ripped my shirt off, when I saw myself. My abs. My pecs. My biceps. I was no longer of average muscle mass, I was of a completely new composition. Every muscle rippled like an ocean, with the power of crashing waves. I felt as though I could lift up a car with only one hand. I was astonished and frightened at what was happening to me. I reached for my phone to call for help, but before I could pick it up, it flew to my hand. I looked at my phone in horror; did I do that? What am I capable of? Suddenly I heard a voice, the voice of my manger, just outside my door, I went outside, but he was nowhere to be seen. I couldn’t understand why I was hearing him, or why he wasn’t here. Instantly, I was outside my store. My manger turned around and greeted me, asking why the shipment of Zoa energy drinks went missing. I was so confused and disoriented that I didn’t answer him. He went on about cameras, and corporate policy, and customer satisfaction, and why he had to let me go. I was suddenly jolted back to reality, and looked at him in a way that I had never looked at anything before. “You’re Fired,” he said. I raised my eyebrow.   My manager is no longer here. Nor the store, or any customers, or employees or product. There is just me. And I feel everything. And I see everything. And I hear everything. And I am everything.

Do you want to experience the thrill of being dropped onto a deserted island with nothing but your wits and a frying pan? Then PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is the game for you!  In PUBG, you'll join 99 other players in a race to be the last person standing. You'll spend your time scavenging for weapons and supplies, hiding in bushes, and praying that the circle doesn't shrink too fast and force you into a deadly game of bumper cars with other players.  One of the game's highlights is the variety of weapons and vehicles available. From shotguns to sniper rifles, from motorcycles to boats, you'll have everything you need to survive the island. And if you're lucky enough to find a frying pan, you can use it to block bullets and cook up a mean omelette.  But don't get too comfortable, because you never know when a hacker will teleport behind you and shoot you in the head from 100 yards away. Or when you'll accidentally throw a grenade at your own feet and blow yourself up.  The game's graphics are also top-notch, with stunningly realistic trees and rocks that you'll spend hours hiding behind, waiting for the perfect moment to strike. And the sound design is equally impressive, with every gunshot and explosion making you feel like you're really in the middle of a warzone.  In conclusion, PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS is a game that will test your survival skills, your reflexes, and your ability to handle stress-induced heart palpitations. But if you're looking for a fun and intense gaming experience, it's definitely worth checking out. Just be prepared to spend hours crawling through grass and getting sniped from across the map!

Ingredients:  6 tablespoons unsalted butter  1/2 cup white sugar  1/2 cup brown sugar  1/4 cup water  1/4 teaspoon cinnamon  1 pinch salt  5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced  1 pastry for double-crust pie  Directions:  Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).  Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.  Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.  Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.  Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.  Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Title: The Pioneer of Battle Royale Madness!   Review: PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds (PUBG) is the game that popularized the battle royale genre, offering intense, large-scale PvP action in a constantly shrinking battlefield. With its realistic gunplay, vast maps, and heart-pounding final circles, PUBG delivers a unique and thrilling experience that keeps you coming back for more.  Gameplay: 9/10 PUBG's gameplay revolves around the simple yet addictive concept of being the last person or team standing in a match of up to 100 players. The realistic gunplay and wide variety of weapons and attachments make combat satisfying and rewarding. The game's pacing can range from slow and tactical to chaotic and fast-paced, ensuring that no two matches are ever the same. The addition of various vehicles adds another layer of strategy and excitement to the game.  Graphics: 8/10 The visual presentation of PUBG has come a long way since its early access days, with detailed environments, improved textures, and better optimization. The game's various maps offer diverse landscapes and settings, each with its own unique challenges and opportunities. While the graphics may not be the most cutting-edge, they effectively serve the game's purposes and contribute to the overall experience.  Sound: 9/10 Sound design is crucial in PUBG, as listening for enemy footsteps, gunfire, and vehicles can be the difference between life and death. The game excels in this area, with realistic and immersive audio that puts you right in the heart of the battle. The addition of a minimalistic, tension-building soundtrack during crucial moments enhances the experience even further.  Performance: 7/10 PUBG's performance has improved significantly since its early days, but it can still be demanding on some systems. Occasional server issues and lag can be frustrating, but these instances have become less frequent over time. Continued updates and optimizations have helped to make the game more accessible and enjoyable for a wider range of players.  Community: 8/10 PUBG's community is large and diverse, with players from all around the world. There is a healthy competitive scene, and the majority of players are friendly and sportsmanlike. However, as with any popular online game, there are occasional toxic players or cheaters, but the game's developers have been proactive in addressing these issues.  Overall: 8.5/10 PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds is a thrilling and addictive battle royale experience that offers tense, large-scale PvP combat in a variety of settings. While it may not be perfect in terms of performance and graphics, its engaging gameplay, realistic gunplay, and diverse maps make it a must-play for fans of the genre. If you're looking to test your skills in a high-stakes, last-man-standing showdown, PUBG is the game for you.

PUBG is like the Hunger Games, but instead of teenagers fighting to the death, it's a bunch of gamers fighting for chicken dinner. And let's be honest, the chicken dinner is the only reason we're all here.  The game starts with you parachuting onto an island with 99 other players, and the objective is simple: be the last one standing. But of course, it's never that easy. You have to scavenge for weapons and gear while avoiding getting shot by other players. And if you're lucky enough to survive long enough, you'll eventually find yourself in a tiny circle with the remaining players, and it's like a dance-off where the winner gets to live.  The weapons in PUBG range from pistols to assault rifles, but let's be real, the only weapon that matters is the frying pan. Not only can you use it as a melee weapon, but it can also deflect bullets, making it the ultimate weapon for survival. Plus, it's hilarious to see someone get killed by a frying pan.  The game also has vehicles, which are both a blessing and a curse. Sure, you can drive around and run over other players, but you can also end up getting stuck in a ditch or driving into a tree like a drunk teenager.  The graphics in PUBG are... not great. It's like playing a game from the early 2000s, but with more grass. But let's be honest, we're not here for the graphics. We're here for the adrenaline rush and the sweet, sweet taste of victory.  And finally, the community. It's like a never-ending battle royale of insults and rage. The chat is filled with people screaming into their mics and calling each other names, but it's all part of the fun.  In conclusion, PUBG is like a game of Russian roulette. You never know if you're going to survive or end up being the first one to die, but at least you get to try again... and again... and again. And who knows, maybe one day you'll get that chicken dinner and feel like a true champion.

The concept of this game is definitely cross-era, and the team behind it keeps creating new content for us, which is not common to see for a six-year-old game. However, if you ask me if it's good if I think that my 1,000 hours spent on it is worth it? Emmm..., [b]not really[/b].  But the problem isn't on the game itself, instead, it's mainly the connection between the dev team and the community. From the first day this game has launched, there always has been a huge amount of hackers and cheaters destroying anyone else's gaming experience. But we didn't see any improvements on the anti-cheat! All we get is BattleEye, Wellbia, more and more anti-cheat software solutions have been integrated, no matter if they are the actual cause but bringing more and more bugs to the game!  There are so many things that could be fixed in the game right now. The "[i]Lost connection to host[/i]" error when opening the inventory, getting "[i]A critical anti-cheat process is not running properly[/i]" when launching the game, overly hard - or sometimes even impossible to get back to the match after disconnecting, with the error "[i]Client not responding[/i]", just to name a few. The bugs we reported, the support tickets we opened, ended up with no responses. We just feel getting ignored.  Anyways, there is still so much Krafton can do to this game to make it better.
